Hi Sergio and Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a procurement hold point before we can finalize the DPA: our security team requires explicit written approval for any onward transfers to downstream subprocessors that will process EU personal data.

We intend to route certain FinPulse EU telemetry (anonymized IDs + usage events) through DataShield (ops@datashield.io) for enrichment and fraud scoring. DataShield is a third-party vendor and will store processed outputs in their environment. Before we proceed, our legal/security team needs: 1) confirmation that Redwood has onboarded DataShield as an approved subprocessor or explicit permission to onward-transfer for FinPulse data, 2) the vendor list and dataflow matrix showing where EU data will go, and 3) details on whether a sandbox/test environment will be used and how keys/segregation are handled.

Can you confirm by EOD tomorrow if Redwood can: a) approve onward transfer to DataShield under existing SCCs/DPA, or b) provide a scoped exception and controls (e.g., separate keying, dedicated project, canary limits) we can attach to our procurement record?

Appreciate a quick turn — procurement is on a tight schedule.

Thanks,
Sarah Lim
Sr. Procurement Manager
FinPulse

Sarah — thanks for the note and the clear list. Looping in Neha (Privacy) and Karthik (Security) to scope the request.

High level: we do not currently list DataShield as a contracted subprocessor for EU personal data in the standard roster. We can either: (1) add them as a subprocessor (requires contract addendum + SOC 2 evidence + update to roster and notifications), or (2) approve a scoped onward-transfer for FinPulse only with technical mitigations (sandboxing, separate keys, restricted retention) while contract is finalized. Option 2 is something we can typically do for enterprise customers on a case-by-case basis.

To proceed we need the following from you (or DataShield):
- precise data types (PII vs pseudonymous IDs vs telemetry payloads) and retention requirements
- the vendor’s SOC 2 Type II report or SIG/CAIQ answers (redacted ok)
- a dataflow matrix showing data movement from Redwood -> DataShield -> any downstream (if applicable)

Can DataShield drop a single archive with the vendor roster + a short SOP for sandboxing? If yes, we can review and propose a set of conditional controls (e.g., separate project, limited retention, dedicated key per FinPulse, max record count for canary).

If you want the fast path, option 2 (scoped onward-transfer approval) is likely quickest — we would still require signed DPA redline and proof of SOC2 within the next 30 days.

Sergio
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
